Methanol ($	ext{CH}_3	ext{OH}$) contains only single bonds and non-bonding electron pairs on oxygen, so it undergoes **$ oldsymbol{\sigma \rightarrow \sigma^*}$** and **$ oldsymbol{n \rightarrow \sigma^*}$** transitions.

Methyl chloride ($	ext{CH}_3	ext{Cl}$) contains carbon-chlorine single bonds and non-bonding electrons (lone pairs) on the chlorine atom, so it undergoes **$ oldsymbol{\sigma \rightarrow \sigma^*}$**, **$ oldsymbol{n \rightarrow \sigma^*}$**, and additionally **$ oldsymbol{n \rightarrow \sigma^*}$** or **$ oldsymbol{n \rightarrow \pi^*}$** (due to halogen heteroatom lone pairs shifting absorption to slightly longer wavelengths compared to alcohols).
proTip: Mention both $\sigma \rightarrow \sigma^*$ and $n \rightarrow \sigma^*$ transitions as they are common for saturated organic molecules with heteroatoms.
